Oregon FIA calibration data: training sites

Source: R/data.R
fia_obs_dt.Rd

A ready-to-fit sample of the US Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) network in Oregon: 200 training sites (fia_*_dt / fia_init_trees) and 200 disjoint holdout sites (fia_*_test) that are never seen during fitting, so a model fit on the training tables can be scored genuinely out of sample. The tables are already in FINN's input format – IDs resolved, species re-indexed 1..K – so they go straight into fit() / simulateForest() without makeObsData() or resolveSiteIDs(). The D-Fit_to_FIA and E-Mortality vignettes are the worked examples.

Usage

fia_obs_dt

fia_obs_test

Format

fia_obs_dt and fia_obs_test: one row per site x year x species (4400 rows, 14 columns). The year-0 initial state is in fia_init_trees / fia_init_test.

siteID, year

integer site index (1..200) and the years since the site's first inventory (10, 20; 21 or 22 for one site each).

period_length

years since the previous inventory (10; 11 or 12 for the late inventory): the window over which the simulation is aggregated before it meets the observation.

species, species_name

species index 1..11 and its name; "other" pools the species outside the 98 % most abundant stems.

ba

living basal area, m2 – the mean over the site's patches (0.06 ha each; makeObsData(aggregate_by_site = TRUE)).

trees

living stems, mean per patch (hence fractional).

dbh

mean diameter at breast height of living trees, cm (NA when there are none).

growth, growth_n

mean annual relative dbh growth rate of the survivors, (dbh / dbh_before)^(1 / period_length) - 1 per tree (tree-weighted over patches), and the number of trees behind it.

n_at_risk, n_died, mort

trees alive at the start of the interval and how many of them had died by its end, summed over patches, and the annual mortality rate 1 - (1 - n_died / n_at_risk)^(1 / period_length). The binomial mortality loss scores mort weighted by n_at_risk.

reg

recruits over the interval, trees per hectare (mean over patches).

An object of class data.table (inherits from data.frame) with 4400 rows and 14 columns.

Source

A seeded subsample of Oregon plots of the US Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) database, with WorldClim bioclimatic variables attached per plot. The preparation script and the provenance of the source tables are in the package repository (dev/make_extdata.R, data-raw/README.md).

Details

All nine objects are data.tables. Attach data.table to use its [ semantics on them, and data.table::copy() one before modifying it by reference (:=), as with any package dataset.

The tables are on an annual time axis: one simulation step is one year. The first inventory (2001-02) is the initial state, year 0; the two remeasurements are observations at the number of years since it, 10 and 20 (21 for one training site and 22 for one holdout site, whose third inventory came late), each with period_length, the years since the previous inventory. Growth and mortality are yearly rates; fit() compounds the simulated yearly rates of the period_length years before each inventory into the same per-year rate before comparing, and compares reg with the recruits simulated over those years. The trees behind the mortality counts are in fia_tree_dt. Before FINN 0.2.0 the tables had one step per ten-year interval (year 1 and 2, rates over the interval); makeObsData(rates = "interval") and resolveSiteIDs(time_axis = "census") still build such tables.

See also

fia_env_dt, fia_init_trees, fia_tree_dt, fia_species_dt

Other fia datasets: fia_env_dt, fia_init_trees, fia_species_dt, fia_tree_dt

Examples

library(data.table)
fia_obs_dt[year == 10, .(sites = uniqueN(siteID), ba = mean(ba)), by = species_name]
#>                species_name sites          ba
#>                      <char> <int>       <num>
#>  1:   Pseudotsuga menziesii   200 0.726985711
#>  2:         Pinus ponderosa   200 0.184966585
#>  3:          Pinus contorta   200 0.024908897
#>  4:          Abies concolor   200 0.055690344
#>  5:           Abies grandis   200 0.054632263
#>  6:      Tsuga heterophylla   200 0.056597997
#>  7:       Tsuga mertensiana   200 0.015395718
#>  8: Lithocarpus densiflorus   200 0.010621666
#>  9:             Alnus rubra   200 0.013027215
#> 10:          Abies amabilis   200 0.006718681
#> 11:                   other   200 0.123505996
# the observation windows: inventory year x interval length, sites
unique(fia_obs_dt[, .(siteID, year, period_length)])[, .N, by = .(year, period_length)]
#>     year period_length     N
#>    <int>         <int> <int>
#> 1:    10            10   200
#> 2:    20            10   199
#> 3:    21            11     1
